messages:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected — control-plane auth-proxy errors in us-west2. Console logins failing (502). Alerts: auth-proxy upstream 502 x5000, control-plane API 5xx spike. https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alert/1721
Alex P: seeing 502 when visiting console, and SDK requests returning 401/502 intermittently. Confirmed from my laptop and synthetic checks.
Priya S: looking at auth-proxy logs — a bunch of upstream timeouts to auth-db replica 2 in us-west2. Latency to that DB jumped from 20ms -> 500ms around 15:42 UTC.
Jordan L: starting failover runbook now. Goal: shift control-plane traffic off us-west2 to us-west1 and eu-west1 where capacity exists. Pausing all config rollouts. @oncall please ack.
Dave M: recommend setting GLB weight for control-plane: set us-west2=0, us-west1=70, eu-west1=30. Also disable autoscaler for nodes in us-west2 so it doesn't keep creating new pods into the churned region.
Emily R: status page draft: "Investigating login and API errors affecting some customers in us-west2. Traffic is being shifted; engineers working on mitigation." I have the page ready to publish once @Jordan L confirms action.
Alex P: quick check — are dedicated customer endpoints hitting the same control plane path? We may need to notify Dedicated customers about degraded routing.
Priya S: yes some Dedicated control-plane proxies in us-west2 are fronting customer endpoints. They should failover with the same GLB change but we should call out potential cache rewarm.
Jordan L: executing GLB update now. Command: 
```
# update weights
curl -X POST https://glb-api.internal/v1/update -d '{"service":"control-plane","weights":{"us-west2":0,"us-west1":70,"eu-west1":30}}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $GLB_TOKEN"
```
Jordan L: GLB update submitted — response 200. Propagation in progress (estimated 45s).
deploy-bot: GLB update job 98432 started by Jordan L — propagation stage 1/3.
Alex P: seeing initial drop in 5xx on synthetic probes. Console still showing auth errors for some sessions (likely expired sessions when backend changed).
Priya S: auth-db replica in us-west2 still showing I/O stalls and high disk wait — filing incident against storage team. Putting a sticky on db-replica-2.
Dave M: autoscaler for us-west2 paused. Command ran: `kubectl scale --replicas=0 hpa/auth-proxy -n controlplane` (patch in progress).
Alex P: note: tokens minted during the brief failover might be invalidated for some users — will require re-login. Add to status page.
Emily R: status page updated and published: "Login/API errors mitigated; users may need to re-authenticate. Full mitigation in progress. Investigating root cause with storage team."
Jordan L: traffic shift seems to have stabilized control-plane API error rate to baseline. Console POST /login success rate up to 95% from 60%. Still seeing a handful of 502s for long-lived sessions.
Priya S: storage team confirms underlying NVMe on us-west2 replica had firmware hiccup causing transient I/O errors; they have remediated and are running consistency checks.
Alex P: can we bring a small portion of traffic back to us-west2 for canary? Want to avoid thrash while storage heals.
Jordan L: plan: keep primary weight 0 for us-west2 for 60 minutes, then add 5% for canary if metrics stable for 15 minutes. Documented in runbook.
Dave M: cost note — shifting traffic to us-west1 will increase cross-region egress and may bump infra bill this window. Ops: track billing delta for this incident.
Emily R: Customer comms prepared for dedicated customers — sent to CSMs and posted on status page.
on-Redwood user?: (reaction) :thumbsup:
Alex P: small follow-up — a few internal services (console-config-rollout webhook) rely on session affinity to us-west2; we should queue rollouts until affinity resets. Already paused rollouts.
Jordan L: can we mark the incident severity? Proposing Sev2 (partial outage affecting login and API for subset of customers). Thoughts?
Priya S: agree Sev2. I'll own postmortem with storage and infra leads.
Jordan L: OK — capturing timeline. Next steps: 1) storage team completes checks and confirms replica healthy; 2) start 5% canary for us-west2 after 60m stable; 3) re-enable autoscaler after canary; 4) postmortem scheduled.
deploy-bot: GLB propagation complete. Job 98432 status: success.
Alex P: console access returned for most users. Still ask users to re-login if they see issues.
Priya S: marking auth-db replica as "recovering" and running a full binary check — will update in 20m.
Emily R: status page note updated: "Mitigation applied; ongoing health checks. Some users may experience brief re-authentication prompts."
Jordan L: thanks everyone. Assigning postmortem to Priya S. If anything regresses, re-open this thread and re-route traffic.
Alex P: thanks team. :white_check_mark:
Priya S: copying link to runbook and postmortem checklist: https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/control-plane-failover
Jordan L: Incident closed (mitigated) for now — will follow up in postmortem.
Alex P: last check: error rates stable for 30m. Moving to monitoring-only.
Emily R: I'll draft the post-incident customer note.
Priya S: postmortem owner acked.
Jordan L: closing thread.
